observation.visible_scene: A Canon EF 70-200mm f/4.5-5.6 DO IS USM zoom lens stands upright, front element facing up, on a circular reflective platform (a mirror/glass turntable) against a warm amber sunburst background with diagonal light streaks. The lens body stays centered in frame for the whole excerpt; the visible markings include the front-ring text 'CANON', 'DO IS USM', 'LENS MADE IN JAPAN', a green index arc, a silver band reading 'ULTRASONIC', and a side switch panel labeled 'LOCK'. A mirror reflection of the ribbed barrel appears below the lens on the platform.
visible_changes: The lens rotates in place about its vertical axis (spin, not translation): the printed/engraved text and the green arc on the front ring continuously shift their angular position around the circumference.

The side 'LOCK' panel label, upright and left-to-right at the start, appears horizontally reversed ('KCOL') in the later frames, and the front-ring 'CANON' likewise changes apparent orientation, indicating the lens has turned so a different side of the barrel faces the camera.
The lens's mirror reflection on the platform rotates in step with the lens (a reflection, not a separate object).
The camera framing remains essentially fixed on the lens; the circular platform edge and the amber background stay in place.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the spin was already ongoing before this excerpt and whether it completes a full revolution after the last frame (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
What caused or sustains the rotation (no operator or drive mechanism is visible).
uncertain_details: Exact rotation direction and total angle are not directly measurable; the apparent reversal of the labels could be true mirroring of the same text seen from the opposite side or different markings coming into view.
Whether the sunburst background co-rotates with the turntable or is a static backdrop cannot be separated from the lens's own rotation with the available evidence.
The precise moment of transition between upright and reversed label orientation is gradual and low-resolution, so it is reported as an apparent change rather than a discrete event.
